### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4fef271b7199f6c5de5a5acd62ac420ac1a99ef0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a27b25f71a55d34db026e8666ca182194db00f56` — the merge of head `3636ef2743f675dc099c1b558d4fd98f1b3784d2` into base `4fef271b7199f6c5de5a5acd62ac420ac1a99ef0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a27b25f71a55d34db026e8666ca182194db00f56 && git checkout a27b25f71a55d34db026e8666ca182194db00f56
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4fef271b7199f6c5de5a5acd62ac420ac1a99ef0 3636ef2743f675dc099c1b558d4fd98f1b3784d2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4fef271b7199f6c5de5a5acd62ac420ac1a99ef0 && git merge --no-ff 3636ef2743f675dc099c1b558d4fd98f1b3784d2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4fef271b7199f6c5de5a5acd62ac420ac1a99ef0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.

## Contract review

Head-sha: `df3185cf9fce167718393d1e2b79a33b60e7258d`

The value is not echoed here by rule. Isolated at-tier subagent; fed the card (#19088 body, report comment `5749323805`), PR #19313 (body, diff, commits, comments, check runs) and the tree at the head; the dispatch order and the dispatching seat's conclusions were not read. Every dev claim below was re-measured, not inherited. Scratch: the reviewer's `pr-19313/` scratchpad, with a detached worktree of the head built with `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` (exit 0).

Provenance of the head: `GET /pulls/19313` head = `df3185cf9fce167718393d1e2b79a33b60e7258d` on `claude/issue-19088-form-field-scale-ceiling`; REST compare `e6a03e649...df3185cf9f` = ahead 3 / behind 0 with merge base `e6a03e649154252740b8e3534804e7abc453fb5c`; `main` has moved 8 commits since, none touching `packages/spec/src` (only `packages/spec/liveness/*`, `packages/lint`, `packages/metadata-protocol`, two plugins, `scripts/pm`, `ci.yml`). Five files in the diff, as listed by the PR.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The one accept-set movement — judged correct.** `FormFieldBaseSchema.scale` (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:2916`) gains `.max(100)`. Re-measured on the source tree with node v22.22.2, base and head: `scale: 100` PASS both; `scale: 101` PASS at base, `too_big` at `[scale]` at head. The number is the platform's, re-measured by me rather than read: `(1.5).toFixed(101)` and `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 101 })` both throw `RangeError` on this runtime, 100 does not. Consumer route confirmed at the pinned objectui sha `53ded82bf7`: `packages/plugin-form/src/sectionFields.ts:220` copies `scale` onto the runtime field and `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:661-667` hands it to `maximumFractionDigits: scale ?? 20`. Every value the bound now refuses was already a render-time crash; no conforming consumer loses a working input. Nit, comment-only: the second route the PR's comments, the module docblock and the changeset cite ("objectui's spec bridge, `form-view.ts` `mapField`") is not at the pin — objectui retired the spec bridge (`.changeset/retire-spec-bridge-6366.md` at `53ded82bf7`, no `spec-bridge/` tree, no `mapField`); the citation is inherited from `liveness/view.json:325`'s 2026-08-26 measurement at objectui@f7c52e2, and the PR says it did not re-measure across repositories. The measured route carries the premise on its own; the stale name is worth dropping from the changeset before it ships in `CHANGELOG.md`, and it does not move this verdict.

2. **"No published export moves" — verified against the package, not the manifest alone; the claim holds.** `files[]` ships `dist`, `src/**/*.zod.ts` and the tracked artifacts; the new file is `src/shared/scale-ceiling.ts`, not `.zod.ts`. `npm pack --dry-run` at the head: 293 entries, 15 `src/shared/*.zod.ts` present, `scale-ceiling` absent. The `exports` map is 19 fixed keys with no pattern, so no deep import reaches a non-entry file. tsup entries are the 17 `index.ts` files and `shared/index.ts` is an explicit `export *` list without the module. On my own build of the head: no `dist/**/*scale-ceiling*`, no `.d.ts`/`.d.mts` names `MAX_RENDERABLE_SCALE`, no bundle export list names it; the message text is inlined into every entry bundle that reaches `view.zod`/`field.zod`, which is how per-entry self-contained bundling already shipped `field.zod.ts`'s copy. Gates on that build: `check:api-surface` unchanged, `check:api-surface-declarations` unchanged (17 entry points, 5364 declarations), `check:export-origins` current (5228 exports), `check:declaration-map` current — all exit 0. One consequence stated for the record: the tarball's `src/ui/view.zod.ts` now imports `../shared/scale-ceiling`, which the tarball does not carry; the same file already imports six unshipped `../shared/*.ts` siblings (`strict-object`, `visibility`, `editability-boundary`, `section-group-reference`, `retired-key`, `lazy-schema`), so the shipped `.zod.ts` set is reference text, not a compile unit, and this adds no new class. Mechanical floor for `yes` not tripped: no new export, no new key on a published payload. `no (narrowing)` is the criterion-honest declaration; `check-widening-tells --declaration no` re-run by me on the PR diff: exit 0, two files judged with no tell, two NOT MEASURED (changeset, mdx), the test file not a contract source — the dev's partition, reproduced.

3. **The pin — I tried to make it pass vacuously; it does not.** The 7 new cases in `src/ui/view.test.ts` run under vitest project `local` (`include: src/**/*.test.ts`; 466/466 green on the file, the 7 named under `--reporter=verbose`), the file is reached by `tsconfig.test.json` (`check:test-typecheck` OK; the file's debt entry is byte-identical base to head). Five mutations in my worktree, each restored, control 7/7 green afterwards: M1 `field.zod.ts` message `100` to `99` at one site — byte-identity case red. M2 shared `MAX_RENDERABLE_SCALE = 99` — 4 red (accepts-100, says-WHY `/100/`, platform-boundary, byte-identity). M3 `view.zod.ts` `.max()` removed — 4 red (too_big, says-WHY, platform-boundary, byte-identity). M4 one-word drift in the shared message — byte-identity red. M5 `field.zod.ts` loses its own `.max()` — byte-identity red (`there.success` flips true, asserted before the guard). Each `if (!x.success)` body is preceded by `expect(x.success).toBe(false)`, so a passing parse cannot skip an assertion silently; `hereMessage` is `toBeDefined()` before equality, so a missing `[scale]` issue cannot equal `undefined`. M2 shows the platform fact is compared live on every run: the schema boundary is asserted against the primitives' own throw point, never against a trusted literal.

4. **Refusal wording — byte-equal.** `SCALE_UPPER_BOUND_MESSAGE` in `shared/scale-ceiling.ts` derives its three `100`s from the constant; `data/field.zod.ts:849-854` hardcodes them. Evaluated both: 434 bytes, equal; the built probe returns the identical string from `FormFieldSchema` and `FieldSchema` at head. Dark control re-derived at base and head on the source tree: `scale: -1` → `too_small` / "Too small: expected number to be ≥0" (source spells the sign as the two ASCII characters; written here with one glyph to keep angle brackets out of this comment); `scale: 2.5` → `invalid_type` / "Invalid input: expected int, received number" — identical code and identical bytes before and after, on this row and on `FieldSchema`. `precision: 101` parses before and after, pinned by a test; the card excludes `precision` by name.

5. **Coverage inside spec — complete.** Every numeric `scale` declaration in `packages/spec/src` now carries the bound: `data/field.zod.ts:931`, `:1213`, `ui/view.zod.ts:2916`. `ui/view.zod.ts:1264` is the timeline `scale` enum, a different key. No fourth site.

6. **Generated surfaces — current.** `content/docs/references/ui/view.mdx` changes two rows, both renderings of `FormFieldBaseSchema` (`## FormField` Properties, and `### Nested Shape: FormSection.fields[number]`). `check:generated` on my build: all 16 artifacts up to date, exit 0. `json-schema/` is untracked build output. CI on the merge commit: `Type Check · source gates` (authorable-surface, docs, generated reconcile) success, `Spec property liveness` success. Nit: the `.describe()` embeds `0-100` and `100` as literals rather than deriving from the constant, the same shape as `field.zod.ts`'s two describes from #18972; the constant cannot move without the platform pin going red, so the literal cannot drift silently.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/19088-form-field-scale-renderer-ceiling.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `fix(spec)!:` title, `**BREAKING**` banner, the narrowing declaration, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Re-run by me against the branch point: `check-adr-0087-registration --base e6a03e649…` exit 0, `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing]`; `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0 (level axis has no PR payload locally; CI `Check Changeset` is success on the head).

Level — right. A narrowing of a published accept set is BREAKING; under the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major` enforces, breaking ships as `minor` carrying the banner. `patch` would understate it, `major` is refused by the gate, and `skip-changeset` does not hold (`@objectstack/spec` publishes and the runtime accept set changes). Same level, banner and disposition as `.changeset/18972-field-scale-renderer-ceiling.md`, already in the tree for the two sibling sites.

ADR-0087 registration — right, and a migration prescription was genuinely not required. No authorable key is renamed, retired or reshaped, so `objectstack migrate meta` has no spelling to rewrite. The only mechanical FROM → TO would be a clamp to 100, which picks a display precision on the author's behalf — the lenient consumer fallback PD #12 forbids — and there is no working deployment to preserve, because no conforming renderer ever honoured a value above 100. The channel that reaches the author is the parse refusal, which carries the prescription (both primitives, the RangeError, the legal maximum). The category's own mechanical check (no FROM/TO block in the body) holds. The stored-`sys_metadata` blind spot is stated in the marker, not hidden, and is the same one #18972 recorded.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **The dispatch fence's false premise — the dev's call was right; the outcome is acceptable and not this PR's to fold in.** Re-measured: `GET /pulls/19083` merged 2026-09-18T17:48:04Z as `021755abc4d1f915ee7a362a72f3945e4d4ed248`; REST compare `021755abc4...e6a03e649` = ahead 91 / behind 0, so both `field.zod.ts` bounds and the private constant were on `main` at this branch's own branch point. The card's reading (17:15Z the same day) was true when taken; the dispatch restated it stale two days later. The claim's declared file surface (`view.zod.ts` plus its tests) is the coordination instrument between parallel seats and the seat that issued the fence owns its revision; widening the surface unilaterally — even for an expired reason — is the move the card itself names as the failure. The dev neither widened nor stayed silent: the expiry is measured and reported in the body, the report and on the card. The cost is one duplicated constant pair held byte-equal by a pin shown above to fail in both directions (M1, M4, M5); no contract, export or gate depends on which file declares the number.

2. **`open_questions[0]` — retire `field.zod.ts`'s private copy? Answered: C, then A.** Fold the two-line delete-and-import into whichever card next holds `data/field.zod.ts`; if nothing claims that file within the round, dispatch A as its own bounded card. Either way no published export moves (`check:api-surface` is unchanged because the module-private symbols were never on it) and no contract review is owed; the existing byte-identity pin keeps holding across the move. B is the honest floor meanwhile — the pin already carries the drift risk. Routed to the PM loop as the scheduling decision it is; no contract question stays open.

3. **`noted, not filed`, one by one.**
   - Three recordings of the ceiling (shared module, `field.zod.ts`'s private copy, `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:994` `MAX_FORMULA_SCALE = 100`): correctly noted, correctly not filed. The first pair is item 2. The objectql copy is structural (`objectql` depends on `spec`, not the reverse) and, with spec refusing above 100 first, its skip-rounding branch is unreachable from spec-valid metadata, so a drift there cannot produce a divergent reading of valid input.
   - `precision` bounded on one arm (`CurrencyConfigSchema` `.max(10)`) and unbounded on two: correctly noted, correctly not filed. The card excludes it by name, the renderer-ceiling argument does not reach a total-digit count, and a test pins `precision: 101` parsing so the omission is measured. PD #10 files on evidence — a repro, contract text or an authoring trap — and none is measured here; whoever decides the three `precision` arms decides them together.
   - The fence outlived its reason: correctly noted and correctly routed to the PM loop that cuts the next `field.zod.ts` card — a dispatch-hygiene fact (a premise not re-measured at dispatch time), not a repository defect.
   - (report only) Negative sample for #19099: re-run by me on the PR diff, `check-widening-tells --declaration no` exits 0 with the same partition; correctly routed to #19099.

Check runs on the head at the time of this record: 35 check runs at 2026-09-20T11:06Z — 31 success, 2 skipped, 0 failed, 2 still in progress (`Test Core` aggregate, `Lint & Repo Gates`). The landing seat reads the full set green before queueing; nothing in this review depends on the outstanding shards.
